introduction.title: If
introduction.explanation: An If card checks the world first, then picks what to do.

realWords.text: An If card is an if statement. The question in its round brackets is called the condition. The lines in the curly brackets run only when the condition is true.
Otherwise is else. The lines after else run when the condition is false, so exactly one of the two parts runs, never both.
Repeat until is a while loop. It checks its condition before every time round and stops when the condition is false. Until blocked is written the other way round: while not blocked.
An exclamation mark means not. It flips true to false and false to true, so !robot.blockedAhead() is true when nothing is in the way.
